Photograph: David J Phillip/AP View image in fullscreen Alex Jones arrives at court in Houston, Texas, on 14 June 2024. Photograph: David J Phillip/AP Texas Texas slashes $50m judgment against Alex Jones over false claim Sandy Hook shooting was hoax Appeals court slashes judgment to $1.5m in a significant legal victory for the rightwing Infowars founder Edward Helmore and agency Fri 21 Aug 2026 12.27 EDT First published on Fri 21 Aug 2026 11.32 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A Texas appeals court has slashed the $50m judgment to $1.5m against Alex Jones, founder of the rightwing platform Infowars , over falsely calling the 2012 Sandy Hook school shooting in Newtown, Connecticut, a hoax. The ruling does not affect a $1.4bn judgment against Jones in Connecticut, but is a significant legal victory for Jones after he and his company, Free Speech Systems, were found liable for damages for claiming the mass shooting didn’t happen. The unanimous opinion issued by the Texas third court of appeals found that Sandy Hook parents Neil Heslin and Scarlett Lewis did not show sufficient evidence that harassment enflamed by Jones’s hoax claims rose to a level that would allow them to exceed the state’s $750,000 cap on damages. Last year, the US supreme court refused to hear an appeal from Jones over the larger award but did not provide a reason for its decision. Jones’s efforts to meet the awards have been subject to legal wrangling. In 2024, Jones dropped a petition and placed himself and his company into bankruptcy, admitting he had to pay the Sandy Hook families. Bankruptcy legal proceedings continue. Jones has fought to retain control of Infowars, the influential rightwing business and platform he founded in the late 1990s that he used to broadcast conspiracy theories – and enrich himself with millions of dollars by marketing herbal supplements in the process. Earlier this year, the satirical website the Onion announced plans to take control of Infowars and turn it into a parody of itself under a leasing agreement provisionally approved by a Texas court. However, a completed deal remains in limbo due to legal appeals. Under a proposed deal with court administrators, Infowars would be leased by Global Tetrahedron, a Chicago -based company that owns the Onion, for $81,000 a month – money that would go toward paying the judgments against Jones . Comedian Tim Heidecker, Infowars’s creative director, said : “It would be just a beautiful joke if we could take this pretty toxic, negative, destructive force of Infowars and rebrand it as this beautiful place for our creativity.” Heslin and Lewis’s six-year-old son, Jesse, was among 20 young children and six educators killed in the 2012 attack on Sandy Hook elementary school in Newtown, Connecticut. The lawsuit and 2022 verdict against Jones marked the first time he was held financially liable for peddling lies about the massacre, claiming it was faked by the government to tighten gun laws. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Around 2-3 times a day Sign up to Breaking News US Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion Jones, who portrayed the lawsuit as an attack on his first amendment rights, conceded during the trial that the attack was “100% real” and that he was wrong to have lied about it. But Heslin and Lewis told jurors that an apology wouldn’t suffice and called on them to make Jones pay for the years of suffering he had put them and other Sandy Hook families through. Jones’s trial attorney, Andino Reynal, had said immediately after the verdict that Jones would appeal against the damages amount, and predicted it would be reduced to $1.5m. Beállítom A kormány szerint a Mészáros Lőrinc-féle cégekkel kötött autópálya-szerződés súlyos magyar és európai uniós jogi aggályokat vet, ezért annak lezárását kezdeményezi – derült ki a pénteken megjelent kormányhatározatból . A Magyar Péter miniszterelnök által aláírt határozat szerint a 2022-ben kötött koncessziós szerződés gazdaságilag hátrányos az állam számára. Ezzel kapcsolatban felmerül a szolgáltatás és az ellenszolgáltatás feltűnő értékaránytalansága, ezért Vitézy Dávid közlekedési miniszternek azonnal tárgyalásokat kell kezdeményeznie a koncesszorokkal a szerződés lezárásáról. A kormányhatározat szerint a szerződés a magyar állam és hét, Mészáros Lőrinchez köthető magántőkealap, a Themis, a Konzum PE, az Opus New Way, az Opus Bridge, a Cronus, a Vesta és a Via között jött létre. A koncesszorok feladata a magyarországi autópályák üzemeltetése, illetve egyes fejlesztések elvégzése volt. A mostani határozat alapján nem szűnik meg azonnal a koncesszió. A kormány a közlekedési és beruházási minisztert arra utasította, hogy haladéktalanul tájékoztassa a koncesszorokat és a koncessziós társaságot a kormány jogi és gazdasági álláspontjáról, majd kezdeményezzen tárgyalásokat. A határozat szerint a kormány célja a szerződésből eredő helyzet rendezése és a jogszerűség biztosítása. Ha a tárgyalások nem vezetnek eredményre, Vitézy Dávidnak intézkedési javaslatot kell tennie a kormánynak a jogviszony lezárására. Magyar Péter miniszterelnök és Vitézy Dávid közlekedési és beruházási miniszter a pénteki kormányszóvivői sajtótájékoztatón jelentette be, hogy a kormány elindítja a 2022-ben indult, 35 évre szóló Mészáros-féle autópálya-koncesszió megszüntetését szolgáló lépéseket. Vitézy szerint a kormány több szempontból jogszerűtlennek tartja a szerződést, így álláspontjuk szerint több indokuk is lenne rá, hogy egyoldalúan felmondják azt. Azonban ilyen esetben egy nemzetközi választottbíróságnak kellene rendeznie az állam és a koncessziós cég (az MKIF Zrt.) közötti jogvitát, ami évekig is eltarthatna, ezért a kormány elkerülné ezt az utat. Ehelyett tárgyalásokat kezdeményeznek a vállalattal, hogy közös megegyezéssel, a lehető leghamarabb felszámolhassák a koncessziót. A kormány döntéséről ebben a cikkben írtunk bővebben. Az MKIF Zrt. a bejelentés után azt közölte, várják, hogy a kormányzat megküldje számukra a hivatalos, írásos tájékoztatást. „Az MKIF Zrt. ennek megismerését követően alakítja ki hivatalos álláspontját, amelyről a későbbiekben tájékoztatja a nyilvánosságot” – írták közleményükben. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c962.text: Figure caption, 'There were so many people, why him?' Yvonne Akinyi remembers the day her husband was shot dead Published 12 October 2026 Three mourners killed when Kenyan police opened fire at a national farewell for former Prime Minister Raila Odinga were not involved in a clash that sparked gunfire, a BBC Africa Eye investigation has found. During an event held last October for people to pay their respects to Odinga, three people were shot dead after mourners attempted to gain access to the VIP section of Nairobi's Kasarani Stadium by force. BBC analysis from inside the stadium shows the victims were each between at least 60m (197 ft) and 160m from the scuffles. Kenya's Interior Minister Kipchumba Murkomen told the BBC that the police action had been "restrained" after the crowd starting throwing stones. In footage analysed by the BBC, it is clear that objects, including plastic chairs, are thrown, but we have no evidence that they included stones. The BBC went through more than 1,500 images and videos to establish the location of those killed in the stadium on 16 October 2025, and also spoke to some of their relatives. Forensic analysis by the BBC suggests an elite police unit responsible for protecting the president may have fired the fatal shots. Kenya's longest serving opposition leader and former prime minister died the previous day while receiving medical treatment in India. He was one of the country's most influential political figures. A year on, Kenya's police watchdog, the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA), is still investigating the deaths and police response and no-one has been held to account. The interior minister defended the police by saying they had been under "so much pressure" after working for many hours non-stop and had been deployed to a new venue at the last minute. "The investigations are being done by an independent police oversight authority, we believe that their findings will help us take appropriate legal action," Murkomen said. Responding to questions about the conduct of police he said: "I don't thinkâ¦ somebody [was] sitting there and saying: 'Shoot now'. It is the judgment of the police officer at the spur of the moment." Image caption, Evans Kiche (l) and Jidah Burka (r) were shot in the head, while Vincent Ogutu (c) was shot in the chest Yvonne Akinyi, who husband was among those killed told the BBC: "The people who we look at to protect us, these are the people that cause us this pain. These are the people that make us to become young widows in this country, young orphans in this county," she said. Odinga's death at 80 prompted an outpouring of grief across Kenya. Thousands gathered at Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport as his body was flown home. The body had originally been due to lie in state at parliament, but the scale of the crowds and fears of a security breach forced a last-minute change of venue to Kasarani Stadium. Officials say they had little time to secure the 48,000-capacity venue, and thousands spilled onto the pitch and into the stands unchecked. After several hours of waiting to see the coffin in 30C heat with no public address system for official updates, a small section of the crowd began throwing objects, including plastic chairs, at officers guarding the VIP pavilion. Police fired live rounds as mourners pushed toward the pavilion. Footage from elsewhere in the stadium shows the crowd remained largely peaceful. Goodbye Raila BBC Africa Eye investigates the killing of three mourners at Raila Odingaâs national farewell Watch on iPlayer Watch on iPlayer Outside the UK watch on YouTube , external In total, three people were killed. One of them was Evans Kiche, a 40 year-old-chef and father to seven children. BBC analysis shows he was around 60m from the confrontation when he was killed by a gunshot wound to the head. The two other mourners killed, Vincent Ogutu and Jidah Burka, were at least 160m away, in the opposite stands, far removed from the pavilion. Autopsy reports confirm that Ogutu died from a gunshot wound to the chest and 42 year-old Burka was fatally shot in the head. Piecing together a timeline of events, BBC Africa Eye identified at least eight police officers operating together, wearing tactical clothing and military camouflage. These officers carry assault rifles, with no visible insignia and faces covered. Their uniforms and movements are consistent with a layer of security assigned to President William Ruto and other VIPs before and after the shooting. At least three officers of this unit appear to fire their weapons. The BBC identified three of them as part of an elite police unit responsible for presidential protection. The BBC cannot establish which bullets killed each victim, and cannot rule out other officers firing inside the stadium. Kenya's National Police Service told the BBC: "There are huge lessons picked from the day's events," which had "formed a fundamental learning curve for a better, more professional application in the future." The IPOA did not respond to a request for comment. Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, The shooting caused panic among the thousands of people inside the stadium Ogutu, a 36-year-old father of three, hadn't planned to go to Kasarani, his wife told the BBC. He was in central Nairobi on the morning of 16 October with friends when they saw the crowds heading to the stadium and decided to join. Within hours, he was dead. His widow Yvonne Akinyi described how the killing upended their family, saying their children were now orphans. As she prepares to mark a year since her husband's death, Akinyi is no closer to understanding why he died while paying his respects at an event organised by the government. "I will just try to be that strong woman. Very strong. But deep inside there is a hole," she said. "It is very painful because sometimes you just sit down and ask yourself. At Kasarani there were so many people, so many of them. Why him."
